canaanite_resheph.name: Loose plague-arrows that strike down the host
canaanite_resheph.notes: Resheph spreads pestilence and sudden death by shooting his arrows into a population; in Egypt he was likewise a god of plague and battle.

canaanite_resheph.name: Guard the warrior and the chariot in battle
canaanite_resheph.notes: Adopted in New Kingdom Egypt as a war-god and patron of horses and chariotry, invoked for protection by pharaohs such as Amenhotep II.

canaanite_kotharot.name: Bless the bridal bed and ensure conception
canaanite_kotharot.notes: Invoked as a band (hbl) at the wedding of Nikkal and Yarikh in KTU 1.24 and at human weddings to secure a fruitful union and the birth of a son.

sources.reference: Ugaritic text KTU 1.24 (Hymn of Nikkal and the Kotharat)

canaanite_shapshu.name: Behold all that passes on earth by daylight
canaanite_shapshu.notes: As the eye of heaven the 'Torch of the Gods' surveys the whole world and so serves as witness, messenger of El, and arbiter of disputes among the gods.

cherokee_unelanuhi.name: Apportion the day and measure out time
cherokee_unelanuhi.notes: Her name Une'lanu'hi, 'the Apportioner', marks her as the divider of the day as she crosses the sky vault from east to west.

sources.reference: James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900)

cherokee_moon.name: Shed the mild light that humans smile upon
cherokee_moon.notes: Crossing the night sky in the west, the Moon gives a gentle light at which his 'younger brothers' (humankind) smile, unlike the fierce glare of his sister the Sun.

sources.reference: James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900), 'The Daughter of the Sun'

chinese_change.name: Become an immortal and dwell on the moon
chinese_change.notes: Having swallowed the elixir of immortality, Chang'e rises from the earth and takes up everlasting residence in the lunar palace.

sources.reference: Mid-Autumn Festival legend of Chang'e and Hou Yi (ChinaHighlights, TravelChinaGuide)

chinese_caishen.name: Bestow riches and ward off financial ruin
chinese_caishen.notes: As the Military God of Wealth (Wu Caishen), Zhao Gongming dispenses prosperity and protects households and businesses from loss; petitioned especially at the Lunar New Year.

chinese_diku.name: Travel by dragon in spring and summer, by horse in autumn and winter
chinese_diku.notes: Sima Qian's Shiji records that after taking the throne Emperor Ku rode a dragon in the warm seasons and a horse in the cold, an emblem of his harmony with the cosmic order.

sources.reference: Sima Qian, Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors

chinese_danzhu.name: Reputed inventor of weiqi (the game of Go)
chinese_danzhu.notes: Tradition holds that Yao devised the game of weiqi to instruct or occupy his unruly son Danzhu, making Danzhu the figure most associated with its origin.

sources.reference: Zhang Hua, Bowuzhi (Records of Diverse Matters), on the origin of weiqi

chamorro_chaifi.name: Forge souls from fire and command wind and water
chamorro_chaifi.notes: A blacksmith-creator dwelling in the fiery mountain Sasalaguan, Chaifi forges spirits out of fire and governs the elements of wind, water and flame.

chewa_chiuta.name: Span the sky as the great bow (rainbow)
chewa_chiuta.notes: The name Chiuta means 'the great bow', identifying the high-god with the rainbow that arches over the earth and signals the gift of rain.

sources.reference: Nyau / Chewa cosmology (Wikipedia, 'Nyau'); A. Werner, Myths and Legends of the Bantu (1933)
James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900), 'The Uktena and the Ulun'suti'

chinese_diku.name: Court music — bells, chimes, pipes and drums made at his order

sources.reference: Lüshi Chunqiu, on Di Ku's invention of music

cheyenne_maheo.name: Grandmother Turtle, who bears the new-made earth

sources.reference: Cheyenne creation account (everyculture.com, 'Cheyenne — Religion and Expressive Culture')

chibiabos.name: Reed flute of the sweetest music

celtiberian_lugus.gloss: the Lugoves / the divine Lugus-triad (dat. Lugovibus)

sources.reference: Votive dedication to the Lugoves by the shoemakers' guild, Uxama (Hispania)

canaanite_resheph.name: Cult of Resheph at Ugarit, Byblos and Apollonia-Arsuf
canaanite_resheph.notes: Resheph was worshipped at Ras Shamra (Ugarit), Byblos and at Arsuf (later Apollonia), and was taken into Egypt under the 18th Dynasty where he received state devotion as a war- and plague-god.

canaanite_yarikh.name: Lunar offerings to Yarikh
canaanite_yarikh.notes: Worshipped at Ugarit with offerings of food and drink, especially at the full moon; he and Nikkal (with Kushuh) receive joint offerings in ritual text KTU 1.111.

canaanite_shapshu.name: Daily solar veneration
canaanite_shapshu.notes: The Torch of the Gods was honoured at the three solar stations of sunrise, noon and sunset.

canaanite_rephaim.name: Marzeah feast of the Rapiuma
canaanite_rephaim.notes: The deified dead were summoned to a banqueting society (marzeah): they journey three days by chariot to the threshing-floor and feast seven days, drinking wine, in rites that linked the living king to his royal ancestors.

chewa_mbona.name: Mbona rain cult at the Khulubvi shrine
chewa_mbona.notes: At the Khulubvi grove in Nsanje the martyr's spirit-hut is annually rebuilt and rain is invoked; a spirit-medium possessed by Mbona and his installed 'wife' Salima mediate his oracles. Inscribed on Malawi's UNESCO tentative list.

sources.reference: J. M. Schoffeleers, River of Blood: The Genesis of a Martyr Cult in Southern Malawi (1992)
UNESCO World Heritage tentative list, 'Khulubvi and Associated Mbona Sacred Rain Shrines'

chaga_ruwa.name: Noon sacrifice to Ruwa
chaga_ruwa.notes: Sacrifices to the sun-high-god were offered at noon; in grave misfortune affecting the chiefdom the whole stomach and intestines of the victim were given to Ruwa, with prayers for harvest and deliverance.

sources.reference: C. Dundas, Kilimanjaro and Its People (1924)

chamorro_taotaomona.name: Reverence of the ancestral taotaomona
chamorro_taotaomona.notes: The ancestral spirits inhabiting banyan groves (trongkon nunu), latte sites and the deep forest are addressed with the formula of permission ('guella yan guello') before entering their places; disrespect (tai respetu) draws their punishment, respect their protection and blessing.

cherokee_selu.name: Green Corn Ceremony
cherokee_selu.notes: The Corn Mother is honoured at the late-summer Green Corn (busk) ceremony, the renewal feast at which the first ripe corn is eaten, old fires are extinguished and rekindled, and the community is purified.

sources.reference: James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900); Cherokee Green Corn (Selu) tradition

attributes.name: Striding smiting-god with raised mace or axe and shield
attributes.notes: Rendered as a bearded warrior in the smiting posture, brandishing a mace or battle-axe and bearing a shield, wearing a tall conical (White) crown.

attributes.name: Gazelle-head at the brow of the crown
attributes.notes: His conical headdress is fronted by the head of a gazelle; in Egypt he was titled the 'gazelle' and 'deer' god.

sacredPlants.name: Orchard fruit-trees (olive, fig, date, apple, almond, walnut)

attributes.name: Seated lady with the lunar crescent
attributes.notes: Following her antecedent Ningal she may be shown enthroned with the crescent of her moon-god husband.

attributes.name: Vast horned serpent, thick as a tree-trunk, scales blazing like fire
attributes.notes: Horned, with scales that glow like sparks and a brilliant diamond crest (the Ulun'suti) on its forehead; only a shot to the seventh spot from the head can kill it.

sources.reference: James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900)
James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900)
James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900)

attributes.name: Lady of the lunar palace
attributes.notes: Depicted as a graceful woman ascending to or dwelling in the moon, often with flowing sleeves and the rabbit at her side.

attributes.name: Black-faced armoured marshal on a black tiger
attributes.notes: Shown as a stern, dark-faced general in armour, mounted on a black tiger, holding a steel whip or golden rod, often with a gold ingot.

attributes.name: Crowned dragon-king of the Eastern Sea
attributes.notes: A great dragon, or a robed and crowned monarch with dragon features, enthroned in the Crystal Palace beneath the eastern waves; commands cloud and rain.

attributes.name: Great antelope mask-structure of Gule Wamkulu
attributes.notes: Embodied as a large basketry antelope figure carried by initiates; the 'Great Mother' of the Nyau, her stylised antelope form veiling her true nature from the uninitiated.

attributes.name: Keeper of the four Sacred Arrows (Maahotse)
attributes.notes: Associated with the Mahuts bundle of four arrows received from Maheo at Bear Butte — two 'Man Arrows' for war and two 'Buffalo Arrows' for the hunt.

attributes.name: Bearer of the Sacred Buffalo Hat (Esevone/Is'siwun)
attributes.notes: Received the horned Sacred Buffalo Hat bundle and the Sun Dance from Maheo, the second great covenant of the Cheyenne beside the Sacred Arrows.

attributes.name: The shield-handed woman who catches arrows
attributes.notes: Her name Chimalman, 'shield-hand', recalls how she caught in her bare hand the arrows Mixcoatl shot at her; she is figured bearing a shield.

sources.reference: Codex Chimalpopoca (Leyenda de los Soles); Manuscript of 1558
